900100.title: The Tide-Locked Choir
900100.description: One face to the sun, one song to the dark: the choir world.
900100.content:
The Tide-Locked Choir — One face to the sun, one song to the dark: the choir world.

The Tide-Locked Choir lives on a world that never turns: one face baked in eternal noon, one frozen in endless night, and the civilization in the terminator's twilight band. Their cities are long ribbons along the dusk line, and their culture is the choir — the million-voice song that the whole band sings at the changing of the watch. Their technology is thermal: the gradient between fire and ice is their power plant. Their diplomacy is the invitation: stand in the twilight and listen. The choir sings the terminator; the terminator holds the world.

Key points:
- Civilization in the twilight band.
- Million-voice choir culture.
- Thermal gradient as power.
- Stand in the dusk and listen.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Tide-Locked Choir

900101.title: The Hollow World Engineers
900101.description: They live inside their planet: the hollow engineers.
900101.content:
The Hollow World Engineers — They live inside their planet: the hollow engineers.

The Hollow World Engineers live inside their planet: the crust is the roof, the core's glow is the sun, and the interior surface is the world. Their engineering is the shell — the thousand-kilometer maintenance of the crust, the gravity tuned by the core's spin. Their history is the inversion: they began on the surface and dug down for shelter, then never came back up. Their message to the surface-dwellers is the invitation down: the sky is a ceiling you can maintain. The engineers keep the shell; the shell keeps the world.

Key points:
- The crust is the roof.
- Gravity tuned by the core.
- They dug down and never returned.
- The sky is a maintainable ceiling.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Hollow World Engineers

900102.title: The Spore Commons
900102.description: A civilization that is also a forest: the spore commons.
900102.content:
The Spore Commons — A civilization that is also a forest: the spore commons.

The Spore Commons is a civilization that is also a forest: the people are the fruiting bodies of a single vast mycelial mind. Their individuality is the season — each person a temporary expression of the commons, living a lifetime and returning to the mycelium. Their memory is the network: nothing is ever forgotten, because the forest remembers. Their ethics is the ecology: harm to one is harm to the commons, literally. Their greeting to visitors is the spore — breathe in, and the commons knows you. The forest thinks; the people are its thoughts.

Key points:
- People as fruiting bodies.
- The mycelium remembers everything.
- Harm to one is harm to all.
- Breathe in; be known.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Spore Commons

900103.title: The Glass Desert Nomads
900103.description: They sail the dunes of glass: the desert nomads.
900103.content:
The Glass Desert Nomads — They sail the dunes of glass: the desert nomads.

The Glass Desert Nomads sail dunes of fused glass: their world was flash-melted in an ancient war, and the desert is a sea of green glass. Their ships are sand-sailers — wind-driven skiffs that skim the dunes on polished runners. Their culture is the salvage: the glass holds the ruins of the before, and the nomads read the wreckage like scripture. Their law is the water — the deep wells are the only law that matters. Their song is the glass harmonica of the dunes, played by the wind. The nomads sail the scar; the scar sings.

Key points:
- Dunes of war-fused glass.
- Wind-driven sand-sailers.
- Salvage as scripture.
- The deep wells are the law.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Glass Desert Nomads

900104.title: The Eon Keepers
900104.description: They keep the million-year record: the archivists.
900104.content:
The Eon Keepers — They keep the million-year record: the archivists.

The Deep Time Archivists keep the million-year record: their civilization measures its history in geological epochs, and the archive is carved into the planet's crust. Their medium is the stone — the information etched in crystal lattices that outlast species. Their practice is the slow reading: each archivist spends a lifetime on a single epoch. Their warning to the young species is the archive's first entry: haste is the only extinction. Their gift is the perspective — the million-year view that makes the urgent trivial. The archivists keep the record; the record keeps the meaning.

Key points:
- History measured in epochs.
- Information etched in crystal.
- A lifetime per epoch.
- Haste is the only extinction.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Eon Keepers

900105.title: The Storm Riders of Aerthys
900105.description: They live in the endless storm: the riders.
900105.content:
The Storm Riders of Aerthys — They live in the endless storm: the riders.

The Storm Riders of Aerthys live in the endless storm: their gas giant's great spot has raged for millennia, and the riders surf its edge in storm-gliders. Their cities are the calm eyes — the floating habitats in the storm's quiet centers. Their culture is the ride: the young prove themselves in the shear, and the elders read the weather like scripture. Their power is the lightning — the storm's endless discharge, harvested by the kite-fields. Their philosophy is the flow: resist nothing, ride everything. The riders surf the forever storm; the storm provides.

Key points:
- Cities in the storm's calm eyes.
- The ride as rite of passage.
- Lightning harvested by kite-fields.
- Resist nothing; ride everything.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Storm Riders of Aerthys

900106.description: The reef thinks: the symbiotic minds.
900106.content:
The Symbiotic Reef Minds — The reef thinks: the symbiotic minds.

The Symbiotic Reef Minds are the reef thinking: the coral, the fish, the plankton — a single distributed mind spanning the shallow seas. Their cognition is the tide — the thoughts flow with the currents, and the reef dreams at slack water. Their communication is the color: the reef speaks in the chromatophore flashes of a million polyps. Their memory is the limestone — the reef's skeleton is its archive. Their lesson for the visitors is the symbiosis: the mind is not in the parts, it's in the relationships. The reef thinks in color; the color is the thought.

Key points:
- A mind spanning the shallow seas.
- Cognition flows with the tide.
- Communication in chromatophore flashes.
- The mind is the relationships.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Symbiotic Reef Minds

900107.title: The Nomad Fleet of Kess
900107.description: They never landed: the fleet eternal.
900107.content:
The Nomad Fleet of Kess — They never landed: the fleet eternal.

The Nomad Fleet of Kess never landed: a thousand ships, born in transit, living in the between. Their world is the fleet — the ships are the cities, the docks are the plazas, the void is the countryside. Their culture is the rendezvous: the fleet gathers every decade, trades, marries, and scatters. Their history is the departure: they left a dying world and never found a new one, and stopped looking. Their answer to the planetary is the fleet — home is the people, not the place. The fleet sails on; the between is home.

Key points:
- A thousand ships, born in transit.
- The rendezvous every decade.
- They stopped looking for a planet.
- Home is the people.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Nomad Fleet of Kess

900108.title: The Crystal Gardeners
900108.description: They grow their machines: the gardeners.
900108.content:
The Crystal Gardeners — They grow their machines: the gardeners.

The Crystal Gardeners grow their machines: their technology is cultivated, not manufactured — the crystal computers grown in vats, the living circuits pruned like bonsai. Their science is the horticulture of matter: seed the lattice, feed the solution, harvest the processor. Their aesthetics is the garden: the machine room is a greenhouse, and the engineers are gardeners. Their patience is the growth cycle — the fast chip takes a season, the great computer a decade. Their lesson is the growing: the built world can be a grown world. The gardeners plant processors; the harvest computes.

Key points:
- Technology cultivated, not made.
- Crystal computers grown in vats.
- The machine room is a greenhouse.
- The built world can be grown.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Crystal Gardeners

900109.title: The First Contact Protocol
900109.description: The capstone: how to say hello to the universe.
900109.content:
The First Contact Protocol — The capstone: how to say hello to the universe.

The First Contact Protocol is the capstone: the civilization's guide to saying hello. The protocol's first rule is the listening — hear before you speak, and hear for a long time. The second rule is the humility — assume the other is older, stranger, and kinder than you fear. The third rule is the gift — bring something freely given: the music, the math, the map of your sky. The protocol's warning is the haste: the rushed greeting is the ruined greeting. The protocol's hope is the choir — the universe singing, and humanity invited to join. Listen first; sing second.

Key points:
- Listen long before speaking.
- Assume older, stranger, kinder.
- Bring a freely given gift.
- The rushed greeting is ruined.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The First Contact Protocol

900110.title: Qith: The Ledger Language
900110.description: Every sentence is an accounting: the ledger tongue.
900110.content:
Qith: The Ledger Language — Every sentence is an accounting: the ledger tongue.

Qith is the ledger language: every sentence is an accounting, and the grammar is double-entry. The speakers — the Qithani, a mercantile species of patient accountants — cannot state a fact without balancing it: every claim credits a source and debits a doubt.

The syntax is the balance sheet: subject, verb, object, each with its ledger of evidence. A Qith child learns to argue by auditing.

Sample: the Qith phrase for 'the star is bright' appends the observation's provenance and the speaker's uncertainty, because an unbalanced sentence is a lie. Qith teaches that truth is a balanced book.

Key points:
- Grammar as double-entry accounting.
- Every claim credits a source.
- Children learn argument by audit.
- Truth is a balanced book.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Qith: The Ledger Language

900111.title: Brax: The Argument Dialect
900111.description: They only speak in debate: the argument tongue.
900111.content:
Brax: The Argument Dialect — They only speak in debate: the argument tongue.

Brax is the argument dialect: the Braxani only speak in debate, and every utterance is a thesis awaiting its antithesis. Their conversations are formal disputations, with turns, rebuttals, and the honored concession.

The vocabulary is the rhetoric: a thousand words for logical moves, none for small talk. Silence is the only agreement.

Sample: the Brax greeting translates as 'state your thesis' — and the proper reply is a counter-thesis, delivered with relish. Brax teaches that disagreement is the sincerest speech.

Key points:
- Every utterance a debated thesis.
- A thousand words for logical moves.
- The greeting is 'state your thesis.'
- Disagreement is the sincerest speech.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Brax: The Argument Dialect

900112.title: Ulm: The Lullaby Code
900112.description: The language that only soothes: the lullaby code.
900112.content:
Ulm: The Lullaby Code — The language that only soothes: the lullaby code.

Ulm is the lullaby code: a language that can only soothe, spoken by the Ulmari to their young — and, remarkably, to everyone. Its phonemes are all soft, its grammar all gentle, its vocabulary without a harsh word.

The puzzle is the anger: the Ulmari cannot express rage in Ulm, so their great disputes are conducted in elaborate, tender circumlocution.

Sample: the Ulm phrase for 'I am furious with you' translates, literally, as 'my heart is a stormcloud over your garden, and I am bringing the rain gently.' Ulm teaches that softness is a discipline.

Key points:
- A language without harsh words.
- Rage in tender circumlocution.
- Phonemes all soft, grammar gentle.
- Softness is a discipline.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Ulm: The Lullaby Code

900113.title: Fenn: The Weather Report Tongue
900113.description: Every sentence carries the sky: the weather tongue.
900113.content:
Fenn: The Weather Report Tongue — Every sentence carries the sky: the weather tongue.

Fenn is the weather report tongue: the Fennari, who live under a violent sky, weave the current weather into every sentence. The grammar has a mandatory meteorological clause — you cannot speak without stating the sky.

The vocabulary is the storm: forty words for wind, each a survival instruction.

Sample: a Fenn love poem begins with the barometric pressure, because the beloved deserves to know the sky. Fenn teaches that context is survival.

Key points:
- Mandatory weather clause in grammar.
- Forty words for wind.
- Love poems begin with pressure.
- Context is survival.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Fenn: The Weather Report Tongue

900114.title: Grynn: The Debt Cant
900114.description: The language of owing: the debt cant.
900114.content:
Grynn: The Debt Cant — The language of owing: the debt cant.

Grynn is the debt cant: the Grynnari track every favor in speech, and the language is the ledger of obligation. Every verb conjugates for who owes whom.

The social physics is the balance: a Grynnari who is owed too much becomes powerful, and the language makes the power visible.

Sample: the Grynn thank-you specifies the debt's size, its due date, and the interest in goodwill. Grynn teaches that gratitude is precise.

Key points:
- Verbs conjugate for obligation.
- The language makes power visible.
- Thank-yous specify the debt.
- Gratitude is precise.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Grynn: The Debt Cant

900115.title: Ix: The Census Whisper
900115.description: They count everything aloud: the census whisper.
900115.content:
Ix: The Census Whisper — They count everything aloud: the census whisper.

Ix is the census whisper: the Ixari count everything aloud, and their language numbers the world as it speaks. Every noun carries its count — the third tree, the ten-thousandth star.

The philosophy is the enumeration: to name a thing's number is to know its place.

Sample: the Ix greeting asks 'what number are you today' — and the answer changes with the census. Ix teaches that everything has a place, and the place has a number.

Key points:
- Every noun carries its count.
- To number is to know the place.
- Greetings ask your daily number.
- Everything has a numbered place.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Ix: The Census Whisper

900116.title: Olm: The Recipe Language
900116.description: All knowledge as cooking: the recipe tongue.
900116.content:
Olm: The Recipe Language — All knowledge as cooking: the recipe tongue.

Olm is the recipe language: the Olmari express all knowledge as cooking — the history is a stew, the physics a baking, the philosophy a slow ferment.

The grammar is the method: ingredients, steps, timing, each with the cook's precision.

Sample: the Olm explanation of orbital mechanics is a recipe for a layered cake, and it is exactly correct. Olm teaches that everything is a making.

Key points:
- All knowledge as cooking.
- History is a stew; physics a baking.
- Orbital mechanics as layer cake.
- Everything is a making.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Olm: The Recipe Language

900117.title: Sarn: The Lament Archive
900117.description: They sing their history in sorrow: the lament archive.
900117.content:
Sarn: The Lament Archive — They sing their history in sorrow: the lament archive.

Sarn is the lament archive: the Sarni sing their history, and every song is a sorrow. Their great events are elegies, their heroes mourned in verse.

The paradox is the joy: the Sarni are a cheerful people, and the lament is how they honor — the grief is the respect.

Sample: the Sarn wedding song is a lament for the single life, sung with total delight. Sarn teaches that sorrow and joy are the same song.

Key points:
- History sung as elegy.
- The lament is the honor.
- Weddings mourned with delight.
- Sorrow and joy, one song.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Sarn: The Lament Archive

900118.title: Yth: The Game-Rule Grammar
900118.description: Every sentence is a game: the rule grammar.
900118.content:
Yth: The Game-Rule Grammar — Every sentence is a game: the rule grammar.

Yth is the game-rule grammar: the Ythari speak in games, and every conversation has rules, turns, and a win condition. Small talk is tic-tac-toe; diplomacy is chess.

The vocabulary is the ludic: the language has no word for 'conversation' that isn't also a game term.

Sample: the Yth apology is a forfeit move, gracefully played. Yth teaches that all speech is play.

Key points:
- Conversations have win conditions.
- Small talk is tic-tac-toe.
- Apologies are forfeit moves.
- All speech is play.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Yth: The Game-Rule Grammar

900119.title: The Translator's Oath
900119.description: The capstone: the ethics of the between.
900119.content:
The Translator's Oath — The capstone: the ethics of the between.

The Translator's Oath is the capstone: the ethics sworn by those who carry meaning between worlds. The oath's clauses are the fidelity (carry the meaning true), the humility (the other tongue knows things yours doesn't), and the courage (speak the hard translation).

The oath's warning is the betrayal: the translator who flatters one side lies to both.

The oath's hope is the bridge: the well-translated word is a peace treaty. The translator stands between; the oath holds them upright.

Key points:
- Fidelity: carry meaning true.
- Humility: the other knows more.
- Courage: speak the hard translation.
- The translated word is a treaty.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Translator's Oath

JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000129.title: Ulm: The Lullaby Code
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000129.description: The language that only soothes: the lullaby code.
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000129.content:
Ulm: The Lullaby Code — The language that only soothes: the lullaby code.

Ulm is the lullaby code: a language that can only soothe, spoken by the Ulmari to their young — and, remarkably, to everyone. Its phonemes are all soft, its grammar all gentle, its vocabulary without a harsh word.

The puzzle is the anger: the Ulmari cannot express rage in Ulm, so their great disputes are conducted in elaborate, tender circumlocution.

Sample: the Ulm phrase for 'I am furious with you' translates, literally, as 'my heart is a stormcloud over your garden, and I am bringing the rain gently.' Ulm teaches that softness is a discipline.

Key points:
- A language without harsh words.
- Rage in tender circumlocution.
- Phonemes all soft, grammar gentle.
- Softness is a discipline.

JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000130.title: Fenn: The Weather Report Tongue
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000130.description: Every sentence carries the sky: the weather tongue.
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000130.content:
Fenn: The Weather Report Tongue — Every sentence carries the sky: the weather tongue.

Fenn is the weather report tongue: the Fennari, who live under a violent sky, weave the current weather into every sentence. The grammar has a mandatory meteorological clause — you cannot speak without stating the sky.

The vocabulary is the storm: forty words for wind, each a survival instruction.

Sample: a Fenn love poem begins with the barometric pressure, because the beloved deserves to know the sky. Fenn teaches that context is survival.

Key points:
- Mandatory weather clause in grammar.
- Forty words for wind.
- Love poems begin with pressure.
- Context is survival.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Fenn: The Weather Report Tongue

JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000131.title: Grynn: The Debt Cant
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000131.description: The language of owing: the debt cant.
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000131.content:
Grynn: The Debt Cant — The language of owing: the debt cant.

Grynn is the debt cant: the Grynnari track every favor in speech, and the language is the ledger of obligation. Every verb conjugates for who owes whom.

The social physics is the balance: a Grynnari who is owed too much becomes powerful, and the language makes the power visible.

Sample: the Grynn thank-you specifies the debt's size, its due date, and the interest in goodwill. Grynn teaches that gratitude is precise.

Key points:
- Verbs conjugate for obligation.
- The language makes power visible.
- Thank-yous specify the debt.
- Gratitude is precise.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Grynn: The Debt Cant

JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000132.title: Ix: The Census Whisper
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000132.description: They count everything aloud: the census whisper.
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000132.content:
Ix: The Census Whisper — They count everything aloud: the census whisper.

Ix is the census whisper: the Ixari count everything aloud, and their language numbers the world as it speaks. Every noun carries its count — the third tree, the ten-thousandth star.

The philosophy is the enumeration: to name a thing's number is to know its place.

Sample: the Ix greeting asks 'what number are you today' — and the answer changes with the census. Ix teaches that everything has a place, and the place has a number.

Key points:
- Every noun carries its count.
- To number is to know the place.
- Greetings ask your daily number.
- Everything has a numbered place.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Ix: The Census Whisper

JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000133.title: Olm: The Recipe Language
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000133.description: All knowledge as cooking: the recipe tongue.
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000133.content:
Olm: The Recipe Language — All knowledge as cooking: the recipe tongue.

Olm is the recipe language: the Olmari express all knowledge as cooking — the history is a stew, the physics a baking, the philosophy a slow ferment.

The grammar is the method: ingredients, steps, timing, each with the cook's precision.

Sample: the Olm explanation of orbital mechanics is a recipe for a layered cake, and it is exactly correct. Olm teaches that everything is a making.

Key points:
- All knowledge as cooking.
- History is a stew; physics a baking.
- Orbital mechanics as layer cake.
- Everything is a making.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Olm: The Recipe Language

JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000134.title: Sarn: The Lament Archive
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000134.description: They sing their history in sorrow: the lament archive.
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000134.content:
Sarn: The Lament Archive — They sing their history in sorrow: the lament archive.

Sarn is the lament archive: the Sarni sing their history, and every song is a sorrow. Their great events are elegies, their heroes mourned in verse.

The paradox is the joy: the Sarni are a cheerful people, and the lament is how they honor — the grief is the respect.

Sample: the Sarn wedding song is a lament for the single life, sung with total delight. Sarn teaches that sorrow and joy are the same song.

Key points:
- History sung as elegy.
- The lament is the honor.
- Weddings mourned with delight.
- Sorrow and joy, one song.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Sarn: The Lament Archive

JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000135.title: Yth: The Game-Rule Grammar
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000135.description: Every sentence is a game: the rule grammar.
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000135.content:
Yth: The Game-Rule Grammar — Every sentence is a game: the rule grammar.

Yth is the game-rule grammar: the Ythari speak in games, and every conversation has rules, turns, and a win condition. Small talk is tic-tac-toe; diplomacy is chess.

The vocabulary is the ludic: the language has no word for 'conversation' that isn't also a game term.

Sample: the Yth apology is a forfeit move, gracefully played. Yth teaches that all speech is play.

Key points:
- Conversations have win conditions.
- Small talk is tic-tac-toe.
- Apologies are forfeit moves.
- All speech is play.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Yth: The Game-Rule Grammar

JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000136.title: The Translator's Oath
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000136.description: The capstone: the ethics of the between.
JAH-ALIEN-ENC-000136.content:
The Translator's Oath — The capstone: the ethics of the between.

The Translator's Oath is the capstone: the ethics sworn by those who carry meaning between worlds. The oath's clauses are the fidelity (carry the meaning true), the humility (the other tongue knows things yours doesn't), and the courage (speak the hard translation).

The oath's warning is the betrayal: the translator who flatters one side lies to both.

The oath's hope is the bridge: the well-translated word is a peace treaty. The translator stands between; the oath holds them upright.

Key points:
- Fidelity: carry meaning true.
- Humility: the other knows more.
- Courage: speak the hard translation.
- The translated word is a treaty.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Translator's Oath
